🌍 Once reached by missionaries, Indonesia now plans to SEND 30,000 of them by 2033.

Indonesia is preparing for a major global outreach effort. Dr. Bambang Budijanto, chairman of the Indonesian Alliance for World Mission (ALUSIA), is helping lead the initiative. Established in 2023, the coalition unites churches and mission organizations with a shared vision of bringing the message of Jesus beyond Indonesia's borders.

"We owe other nations," Budijanto said during meetings with Indonesian pastors in New York and Philadelphia. "God blessed Indonesia with a lot of revival for a purpose."

Indonesia's history of spreading the message of Jesus dates back to the first missionaries in the Maluku Islands in 1534. Today the country is home to approximately 30 million believers, and 534 cities have ongoing 24-hour prayer initiatives known as "towers of prayer."

"How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things!" — Romans 10:15 🙏

ANN/THE JAKARTA POST – Indonesia is facing calls for a bolder climate commitment ahead of the United Nations (UN) climate talks, as the country is sitting at the forefront of the global environmental crisis, with multiple ecological disasters that have triggered public discontent and regional distress.
